title: The old way of saying it
translation: With everything, honestly, it's the old days I miss. Things nowadays just keep getting cheaper and coarser. Even the lovely things a carpenter makes look best in the old style. The wording in old letters is wonderful. And everyday speech keeps getting worse.

People used to say "Lift the carriage!" and "Raise the lamp!". Now they say "Lift it up!" and "Pull it up!". The palace staff should be told "Torchbearers, stand!", and instead people say "Make the torches bright!". The place where the emperor listens to the great sutra lectures should be called "the hall for His Majesty's lectures", and people just say "lecture hall". An old courtier used to say what a shame it all was.
original: {何事|なにごと}も{古|ふる}き{世|よ}のみぞ{慕|した}はしき。
{今様|いまやう}は{無下|むげ}に{卑|いや}しくこそなり{行|ゆ}くめれ。
かの{木|き}の{道|みち}の{匠|たくみ}のつくれる{美|うつく}しき{器|うつはもの}も、{古代|こたい}の{姿|すがた}こそをかしと{見|み}ゆれ。
{文|ふみ}の{詞|ことば}などぞ、{昔|むかし}の{反古|ほうご}どもはいみじき。
ただいふ{詞|ことば}も、{口惜|くちを}しうこそなりもて{行|ゆ}くなれ。
{古|いにしへ}は、「{車|くるま}もたげよ。」「{火|ひ}{掲|かか}げよ。」とこそいひしを、{今|いま}やうの{人|ひと}は、「もてあげよ。」「かきあげよ。」といふ。
{主殿寮|とのもれう}の「{人数|にんず}だて。」といふべきを、「{立明|たちあか}し{白|しろ}くせよ。」といひ、{最勝講|さいしようかう}の{御聴聞所|みちやうもんどころ}なるをば、「{御講|みかう}の{廬|ろ}。」とこそいふべきを、「{講廬|かうろ}。」といふ、{口|くち}をしとぞ、{古|ふる}き{人|ひと}の{仰|おほ}せられし。
literal: In everything, it is only the old times that one longs for.
The modern style seems to be becoming terribly vulgar.
Even the beautiful vessels that craftsmen of the woodworking trade make look delightful in the ancient form.
As for the words of letters, the old scraps of paper are splendid.
Even the words people simply speak seem to be becoming regrettable.
In the old days they said 'Raise the carriage' and 'Lift the light', but people of the present style say 'Lift it up' and 'Hoist it up'.

What should be called, for the Office of Palace Maintenance, 'Torch-bearers, stand', they call 'Make the standing torches white', and the emperor's listening place at the Saishō lectures, which should be called 'the hut of the august lectures', they call 'lecture hut': a person of the old days said that it was regrettable.

notes.quote: 古き世のみぞ慕はしき
notes.text: ぞ … き again: {慕|した}はし becomes {慕|した}はしき. Complaints that language is going downhill are old: this one is from around 1330.
{今様|いまやう}: 'the present style', what is fashionable now. The same word names the popular songs of section 14.
{反古|ほうご}: used paper, old letters and drafts. Here: old letters and drafts.

The text does not say what is wrong with the new forms, only that the old ones were right; commentators are not sure either. English cannot copy the exact differences, so the translation only shows that the wording changed.
{主殿寮|とのもれう}: the palace office in charge of palanquins, lamps, torches, curtains and cleaning.

{最勝講|さいしようかう}: a yearly series of lectures at the palace on the Golden Light Sutra. The complaint is that 'the hut of the august lectures' was shortened to 'lecture hut': shorter, and without the respect.
